newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down as sterling surges higher.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down as sterling surges higher.

text.p: LIFFE grains were forced down in active trade as sterling hit a new six and a half year high against the mark.
Lower prices enticed enough buyers out for the most active wheat contracts to climb off lows by the close.
However, one trader reckoned that sterling's strength would have meant a new test of lows, had not the close intervened.
November was the most active contract on wheat, with 249 of a total 747 lots. It last traded 0.65 stg lower at 82.35 stg, compared with a low of 81.60 stg.
On barley, November was also most active, with 68 of a total 130 lots. It last traded 0.50 stg lower at 78.25 stg, its low.

Sterling leapt above 3.04 marks for the first time in more than six-and-a-half years, drawing strength, along with the dollar, from expectations that a broad European economic and monetary union will be launched in 1999.
